entities.name: Abu Asim Muhammad ben Ahmad
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abū ʿĀṣim al-ʿAbbādī (985–1066), called al-Qāḍī al-Harawī, was a Shāfiʿī judge and jurist from Herat.

He was born into a prominent family in the city of Herat, in what is now Afghanistan, during the Ghaznavid Empire.

Al-Qāḍī al-Harawī played a crucial role in shaping Islamic jurisprudence, particularly in the fields of inheritance, divorce, and child custody.

His works, such as the 'Mukhtasar al-Fiqh al-Shafi'i', had a profound impact on the development of Islamic law and influenced jurists for centuries to come.

Al-Qāḍī al-Harawī's legacy can be seen in the many schools of thought and legal traditions that followed in his footsteps, including the Hanafi and Maliki schools.

This legacy can be seen in the modern-day legal systems of countries that were once part of the Islamic world, such as Pakistan and Indonesia.

As a testament to his enduring influence, al-Qāḍī al-Harawī's works continue to be studied by scholars and jurists around the world.

In the words of the 12th-century jurist and scholar, Ibn Taymiyyah, 'Al-Qāḍī al-Harawī was a pillar of knowledge, whose works will endure for eternity.'
